How this session is built

The gap first, then the new material

Sessions 1 and 2 go back to A1.2.2 — completing the square, and reading the minimum or maximum value and the range off it. That is the one precise gap your intake identified, and it is worth having secure before anything is built on top of it. Sessions 3 to 7 are the new topic: the sum and product of the roots.

Five of the questions in sessions 1–2 are real CSEC Additional Mathematics Paper 1 questions, each labelled with the sitting it came from. Treat those as exam practice rather than reading — they are the closest thing here to the paper you will actually sit.

Session 6, question 19 is the one to slow down for. It connects this whole tutorial back to the discriminant you already know, and shows that completing the square, the discriminant, and the gap between the roots are three views of one thing.

Sessions 1–2 · reading the completed square

For a(x + h)² + k:

  • Turning point (−h, k) — opposite sign to h
  • a > 0 → minimum, range y ≥ k
  • a < 0 → maximum, range y ≤ k

⚠️ The minimum value is k. Where it happens is x = −h. Questions ask for either.

Sessions 3–7 · the two results

For ax² + bx + c = 0 with roots α, β:

α + β = −b/a
αβ = c/a

And back the other way: x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0.

Identities you will build, not memorise

  • α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ
  • 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ)
  • (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ
  • α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β)

Each is derived in the question that uses it. If you can rebuild them you never have to trust your memory of them.
